patch.objective: Diagnosing performance issues: top/htop, load average, memory and swap usage

sources.cite: CompTIA Linux+ (V8), exam XK0-006, launched 2025-07-15: System management 23%, Services and user management 20%, Security 18%, Automation, orchestration, and scripting 17%, Troubleshooting 22%
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-16 for this Linux+ band of a case written for another Linux course. Relevant text: System management covers configuring 'LVM, RAID, partitions, and mounted storage' and reviewing service logs and timers; Troubleshooting covers 'boot, mount, and repair issues' and analyzing 'CPU, memory, I/O' to 'optimize response times'; Files and directories covers permissions and special files. Time synchronization is not named on the page; the objective wording is the course seed's.

Relevant text: 'On modern Linux, the range is -20 (high priority) to +19 (low priority)'; under CFS each unit of difference in nice value 'results in a factor of 1.25 in the degree to which the scheduler favors the higher priority process'; 'on Linux, the nice value is a per-thread attribute'. Read through a summarizing fetch 2026-11-14.

Relevant text: 'renice alters the scheduling priority of one or more running processes'; -p 'Interpret the succeeding arguments as process IDs (the default)'; 'an unprivileged user can only increase the "nice value"'; 'The superuser may alter the priority of any process'. Read through a summarizing fetch 2026-11-14.

Relevant text: kill(1), 'If no signal is specified, the TERM signal is sent' and 'If a process does not terminate after a TERM signal has been sent, then the KILL signal may be used'; signal(7), 'The signals SIGKILL and SIGSTOP cannot be caught, blocked, or ignored'. Both read through summarizing fetches 2026-11-14. That a SIGKILLed PostgreSQL server must run crash recovery on restart is the database's documented behavior after an unclean stop; the minutes it takes here are authored.
